summary: Tag-based access enforcement blocks llm-provisioner creating staging envs in eu-west
description:
Issue summary:
A recent org-wide tag enforcement rollout started rejecting the llm-provisioner service account's environment creation calls in the staging eu-west region. The provisioner fails during IAM/GCP role binding and instance creation with tag-related denies.

Impact:
- Staging environment creation for private-deploy tests in eu-west is blocked.
- Several CI jobs that provision ephemeral clusters for on-call LLM debugging are failing (blocking SRE workflows).
- No customer-facing production impact observed so far, but developer velocity is impacted and staging parity is degraded.

Environment:
- Service: llm-provisioner (internal service responsible for ephemeral env bootstrap for private deploys)
- Regions: eu-west-1 (only region currently failing), us-east-1 appears unaffected
- Affected identities: service principal: provisioner-sa@redwood-prod.iam.gserviceaccount.com and AWS assume-role sessions created by the provisioner for dedicated-provisioning

Steps to reproduce:
1) Trigger ephemeral staging environment creation via the provisioner: POST /provisioner/environments with payload env=staging, region=eu-west-1
2) Provisioner requests a short-lived AWS STS assume-role with session tags and calls GCP Resource Manager APIs to create project-scoped bindings
3) Calls fail with AccessDenied / PERMISSION_DENIED errors referencing tag conditions

Observed behavior (logs):
- AWS: "AccessDenied: User: arn:aws:sts::123456789012:assumed-role/provisioner-role/session is not authorized to perform: iam:TagRole on resource: role/example because tag 'env:team' was missing or mismatched"
- GCP: "PERMISSION_DENIED: request requires tags: 'env:staging' but tag value 'staging' was normalized to 'Env:Staging' by org normalizer and condition failed"

Expected behavior:
- Provisioner should be able to create ephemeral staging envs in eu-west when authenticated and within expected org guardrails. Tag enforcement should not reject canonical service session tags used by internal infra.

Temporary mitigation applied:
- Added a temporary exception rule in the policy engine to allow the provisioner principal to create staging envs in eu-west while we investigate the root cause (see resolution_notes).

Notes on scope:
- Failure appears tied to the new tag-normalizer release (policy-engine v1.9.0) rolled out 2026-03-09.
- Only affects identities that attach tags via STS/session tags rather than those with permanent resource tags.

investigation_notes:
Timeline: policy-engine v1.9.0 rolled 2026-03-09. Several internal services that rely on STS session tags (including llm-provisioner) started failing in eu-west. Reproduced locally by calling assume-role with session tags 'env=staging' -> policy engine rule expected 'env:staging' exactly and performed case-sensitive compare due to a recently-introduced normalization function.
Hypothesis: PR changed normalization to include title-casing for certain tag namespaces which caused mismatch against existing session tags. Affected code paths: policy-engine tag matcher (pkg/tags/matcher.go) and the enforcement lambda that builds IAM conditions for AWS.
Evidence: Related PR with intentional change: github.com/redwood/policy-engine/commit/3b7f9a1. Test runs and e2e showed no failing tests due to missing coverage for session-tagging flows.
Next actions: revert normalization behaviour or make matcher tolerant to lowercase/uppercase variants; add unit tests; identify other services relying on session tags and notify owners.
resolution_notes:
Temporary fix: policy-engine allowlist exception created for provisioner-sa in eu-west (applied 2026-03-11 08:12). This restored staging provisioning and CI.
Permanent fix plan: 1) Revert the normalization change in policy-engine and release v1.9.1 with added unit tests for session tags (owner: Jorge Martinez). 2) Update provisioning runbook to include tag-casing guidance and steps to add emergency allowlists (owner: Aisha Khan). 3) Audit other services that depend on STS session tags and add compatibility tests to the policy-engine test matrix.
Expected ETA for permanent rollback and release: 2026-03-18.
Follow-up ticket created: INT-303304 (tag-normalizer rollback and test coverage expansion).
